notes.title_strength: Punchy contradiction, but it never says 'horizon', so 'never grew' is cryptic to anyone who hasn't just seen the picture.
notes.curiosity: Creates a real 'but it looks bigger?' gap. The single-Moon thumbnail with one width bar doesn't show what 'same' is compared to, so it adds little pull.
notes.complementarity: 'SAME WIDTH' restates the title's 'camera says never grew' instead of adding new information such as the brain or distance angle.
notes.promise_payoff: The camera claim is paid off in about 4 s (2.2-6.4 s), and only with drawn photo frames, not a real same-setting photo comparison.

notes.accuracy: All statements rest on f2/f3, but the description's 'very slightly smaller in the sky' is never said in the video. Leading the thumbnail with '1.5% FARTHER' next to an eye looking at a big Moon invites viewers to mix up real distance with the apparent-distance explanation.
notes.hook_coherence: The opening promise 'actually a bit farther away' and the '1.5% FARTHER' thumbnail match the third sentence (6.6 s), not the first spoken line or the 'CAMERA SAYS SAME' first frame.
notes.promise_payoff: The 'isn't bigger' title is paid off over 0-9.8 s, but the thumbnail's headline number gets one 3.2 s sentence (6.6-9.8 s), and the video never explains what it means.
notes.clickbait_risk: Honest overall. The only risk is the emphasis on the 1.5% figure, which can read as the reason the Moon looks big.

notes.title_strength: Clear but it states the answer outright ('your brain sees it bigger'), so it has little tension to stop a scroll.
notes.curiosity: The answer is already in the title, and the 'FAR AWAY' thumbnail with a small Moon is cryptic: it reads as the trivial 'the Moon is far away'.
notes.accuracy: The title and hedged description are supported (f3, f5, f4), but the thumbnail's 'FAR AWAY' presents the leading hypothesis as settled fact, with no hedge.
notes.thumbnail_readability: The text is readable at 168 px, but the pink brain reads as a blob or cloud and the Moon is small, so the subject is not instantly clear.
notes.hook_coherence: The opening promise matches the first line and the 'CAMERA SAYS SAME' frame, but the brain-led title and thumbnail correspond to content that only starts at 10 s.
notes.promise_payoff: The brain explanation gets about 6.4 s (10.1-16.5 s), and the mechanism is a single sentence; the video never says why the brain judges the horizon Moon farther away.
